svg.title: CausalLab: sharp response bounds expose the monotonicity assumption
svg.desc: Two supplied action-marginal pairs, with endpoint joint witnesses and a monotone witness. Equal marginals permit helped fractions zero to one half, but monotonicity forces zero. Marginals one quarter and three quarters permit helped fractions one half to three quarters and harmed fractions up to one quarter, despite positive mean effect. These are feasible-joint ranges, not confidence intervals.

svg.text: Supplied point action marginals constrain a joint. Extra monotonicity Y1 >= Y0 rules out harmed (1,0).
Each stacked column is an attaining joint witness; two endpoint witnesses span every feasible joint.
p0=P(Y0=1), p1=P(Y1=1). Ranges are sharp for supplied point marginals, not sampling confidence intervals.
All calculations use exact rational arithmetic for the supplied binary-float inputs; displayed values are rounded.
No monotonicity is learned from a positive mean. Synthetic response names do not imply empirical benefit or harm.
